title: yahoofinancer Cookbook: 15 Practical Recipes
text: Evaluate asset risk efficiency computing annualized return, volatility, downside deviation, Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio relative risk-free benchmark rate (RfR_f).
code: prices <- yf_download_prices(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "NVDA", "^GSPC"), period = "2y", interval = "1d")  rf_annual <- 0.04 rf_daily  <- rf_annual / 252  performance_metrics <- prices |>   group_by(symbol) |>   arrange(date) |>   mutate(     daily_return  = (adj_close / lag(adj_close)) - 1,     excess_return = daily_return - rf_daily   ) |>   filter(!is.na(daily_return)) |>   summarise(     trading_days      = n(),     annual_return     = mean(daily_return) * 252,     annual_volatility = sd(daily_return) * sqrt(252),     sharpe_ratio      = (annual_return - rf_annual) / annual_volatility,     downside_vol      = sqrt(mean(pmin(excess_return, 0)^2)) * sqrt(252),     sortino_ratio     = (annual_return - rf_annual) / downside_vol,     .groups           = "drop"   ) |>   arrange(desc(sharpe_ratio))  print(performance_metrics) #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   symbol trading_days annual_return annual_volatility sharpe_ratio #>   <chr>         <int>         <dbl>             <dbl>        <dbl> #> 1 ^GSPC           500         0.173             0.162        0.820 #> 2 NVDA            500         0.368             0.451        0.727 #> 3 AAPL            500         0.204             0.288        0.570 #> 4 MSFT            500         0.115             0.288        0.259 #> # ℹ 2 more variables: downside_vol <dbl>, sortino_ratio <dbl>

code: # 1. Download prices for a single security prices <- yf_download_prices("MSFT", period = "1y", interval = "1d")  # 2. Compute Bollinger Bands, %B, and Bandwidth bb_df <- prices |>   filter(!is.na(adj_close)) |>   arrange(date) |>   mutate(     bb_middle = rollmeanr(adj_close, k = 20, fill = NA),     bb_sd     = rollapplyr(adj_close, width = 20, FUN = sd, fill = NA),     bb_upper  = bb_middle + (2 * bb_sd),     bb_lower  = bb_middle - (2 * bb_sd),     bb_pct_b  = (adj_close - bb_lower) / (bb_upper - bb_lower),     bandwidth = (bb_upper - bb_lower) / bb_middle   )  tail(bb_df |> select(date, adj_close, bb_lower, bb_middle, bb_upper, bb_pct_b, bandwidth), 6) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   date                adj_close bb_lower bb_middle bb_upper #>   <dttm>                  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 2026-08-11 13:30:00      504.     334.      436.     537. #> 2 2026-08-12 13:30:00      492.     338.      440.     543. #> 3 2026-08-13 13:30:00      497.     342.      445.     549. #> 4 2026-08-14 13:30:00      495.     347.      450.     553. #> 5 2026-08-17 13:30:00      480.     353.      454.     555. #> 6 2026-08-18 13:30:00      481.     360.      458.     557. #> # ℹ 2 more variables: bb_pct_b <dbl>, bandwidth <dbl>

code: #' Download Historical Prices #' #' @description #' Fetches historical price data for single or multiple tickers. Note that Yahoo Finance  #' enforces lookback limits on intraday data (e.g., "1m" interval is limited to the last 7 days). #' #' @param tickers Character vector of stock symbols (e.g., \code{c("AAPL", "MSFT")}). #' @param start Date or character string representing the start date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). #' @param end Date or character string representing the end date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). #' @param interval Time between data points. Defaults to "1y" if both `start` and `period` are NULL. #' #' @return A tidy \code{tibble} containing 8 columns: \code{symbol} (character), \code{date} (POSIXct), \code{open} (numeric), \code{high} (numeric), \code{low} (numeric), \code{close} (numeric), \code{adj_close} (numeric), and \code{volume} (numeric). title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: common starting point. Returns data.frame date, open, high, low, close, adjusted close, volume. Tip: interval accepts "1d", "1wk", "1mo" daily, weekly, monthly bars. Use period = "1y" instead start/end rolling window relative today.
code: aapl <- Ticker$new("AAPL")  prices <- aapl$get_history(   start    = "2024-01-01",   end      = "2024-12-31",   interval = "1d" )  head(prices)

what: 2. Fetch prices for multiple tickers at once
title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: Use Tickers class pull several symbols one object. failed symbol skipped gracefully; rest still return.
code: tickers <- Tickers$new(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "AMZN"))  prices <- tickers$get_history(   start    = "2024-01-01",   interval = "1d" )  # symbol column lets you split or filter easily head(prices[prices$symbol == "MSFT", ])

what: 3. Plot cumulative returns for a portfolio
title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: Pairs naturally recipe 2. Normalises stock 100 start date can compare apples apples.
code: library(ggplot2)  tickers <- Tickers$new(c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL")) prices  <- tickers$get_history(start = "2024-01-01", interval = "1d")  # compute cumulative return indexed to 100 prices <- prices[order(prices$symbol, prices$date), ] prices$cum_return <- ave(   prices$close,   prices$symbol,   FUN = function(x) x / x[1] * 100 )  ggplot(prices, aes(x = as.Date(date), y = cum_return, colour = symbol)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(     title  = "Cumulative return (indexed to 100)",     x      = NULL,     y      = "Index value",     colour = NULL   ) +   theme_minimal()

text: regular_market_price reflects last traded price market hours (closing price outside hours). history call needed. many tickers , use market summary loop Tickers object. get_market_summary() returns snapshot major indices.
code: aapl  <- Ticker$new("AAPL") tsla  <- Ticker$new("TSLA")  cat("AAPL:", aapl$regular_market_price, "\n") cat("TSLA:", tsla$regular_market_price, "\n") get_market_summary()

what: 5. Validate symbols before a bulk download
title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: Passing bad ticker Tickers wastes network call can produce confusing empty data.frames. Run validate() first.
code: symbols <- c("AAPL", "NOTASTOCK", "MSFT", "XYZXYZ")  good <- validate(symbols)  # returns the subset that Yahoo Finance recognises cat("Valid symbols:", paste(good, collapse = ", "), "\n")  tickers <- Tickers$new(good) prices  <- tickers$get_history(start = "2024-01-01", interval = "1d")

what: 6. Pull a key metrics snapshot for stock screening
title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: key_stats surfaces financial ratios — trailing P/E, forward P/E, price--book, enterprise value, — named list. Flatten one-row data.frame easy comparison across tickers.
code: symbols <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "META")  stats <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {   t   <- Ticker$new(sym)   ks  <- t$key_stats   data.frame(     symbol       = sym,     pe_trailing  = ks$trailingPE,     pe_forward   = ks$forwardPE,     price_book   = ks$priceToBook,     profit_margin = ks$profitMargins,     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) })  do.call(rbind, stats)

title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: income_statement() (via financials) returns data.frame annual quarterly income statement items. Use lapply build cross-company comparison table.
code: symbols <- c("AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL")  revenue <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {   t  <- Ticker$new(sym)   fs <- t$income_statement(frequency = "annual")   if (is.null(fs) || nrow(fs) == 0) return(NULL)   # most recent year   row <- fs[1, , drop = FALSE]   data.frame(     symbol       = sym,     year         = format(as.Date(row$asOfDate), "%Y"),     total_revenue = row$TotalRevenue,     net_income    = row$NetIncome,     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) })  do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), revenue))

title: yahoofinancer — Recipes
text: Combines several recipes tidy dplyr pipeline: validate symbols, fetch key stats, filter criteria, rank metric. Note: %||% null-coalescing operator rlang (define locally: `%||%` <- function(, b) (.null()) b else ).
code: library(dplyr)  # candidate universe symbols <- validate(c(   "AAPL", "MSFT", "GOOGL", "META", "AMZN",   "NVDA", "TSM",  "ASML", "ADBE", "CRM" ))  # fetch stats for each stats <- lapply(symbols, function(sym) {   tryCatch({     t  <- Ticker$new(sym)     ks <- t$key_stats     data.frame(       symbol        = sym,       pe_forward    = ks$forwardPE      %||% NA_real_,       price_book    = ks$priceToBook    %||% NA_real_,       profit_margin = ks$profitMargins  %||% NA_real_,       revenue_growth = ks$revenueGrowth %||% NA_real_,       stringsAsFactors = FALSE     )   }, error = function(e) NULL) })  screen <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), stats))  # screen: profitable growth stocks trading below P/B of 15 screen |>   filter(     profit_margin  > 0.15,     revenue_growth > 0.10,     price_book     < 15   ) |>   arrange(pe_forward) |>   select(symbol, pe_forward, price_book, profit_margin, revenue_growth)
